question: Jyoti Prasad Agarwala was a music composer popularly called 'Rupkonwar' in the state of ______.
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Assam.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rupkonwar Jyoti Prasad Agarwala**

 
 
• **​**He was a celebrated Assamese playwright, songwriter, poet, writer, and filmmaker.
 
• His creative vision and prolific output have made him an icon of Assamese culture.
 
• He actively participated in the **Indian independence movement**, which led to his imprisonment for fifteen months in 1932.
 
• He established the Chitraban Studio at the Bholaguri Tea Estate and embarked on creating **Assam's first film, "Joymoti"**, based on a play by **Laxminath Bezbarua.**
 
 
• The film was released in 1935 and depicted the heroic **Ahom princess Sati Joymoti**, who was imprisoned and tortured by a repressive Ahom swargadeo.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• His death anniversary, **January 17**, is observed as **Silpi Divas (Artists' Day)** in his honour.

 - Notable works include short stories like "Rupohi," "Bogitora," "Xontora," and more.

 - His novel "Amar Gaon" and other books like "Jyotidhara" and "Background of Assamese Architecture" showcase his diverse interests.

 - As the Rupkonwar of Assamese culture, he left an indelible mark on Assam's artistic landscape.
